rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Peek at the next module before adding a second exercise.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no exercise added on either side: M3 lists four `[Exercise:]` lines (L33-41), M4 two (L39,41); M3 close L109 and M4 open L8-16 agree.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Between-module reading appears in two places.
rules_evaluated.evidence: FORWARD (M3 close -> M4 open): earn-the-trust.md L93-97 `## Bring to Module 4` (task) and L99-104 `## Pre-read before Module 4` (da Costa, framing 'when generation outruns judgment, the human becomes the stage everything else waits on'). run-the-first-experiment.md L8-10 restates the task line (L10 bold 'A real slice you'd send off rather than nudge bit by bit. Bigger than a typo-fix, smaller than a big epic.' vs M3 L95) and L14 restates the same da Costa URL with a send-off-tied framing. Harm the rule prevents: a student finishing M3 unaware of the homework, or arriving at M4 unreminded; absent. BACKWARD (M4 open -> M3 close): L8 'The scoped task you picked as homework' resolves to M3 L95; L14 da Costa resolves to M3 L104; L12 supplementaries and L16 Horthy ('in the gap after Module 1') are not claimed as M3-sourced, so no orphan. Closest to violating: L14 framing differs from M3 L104 in wording; the rule asks same links plus one-line framing, not identical framing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cross-module artefact contracts must be explicit at both ends.
rules_evaluated.evidence: M3 produces (L182-188 table): ADR at repo ADR convention default `docs/adr/NNNN-slug.md` (prompt threat-model-with-stride-3 saves it to that path), skill at `~/.claude/skills/test-strategy/SKILL.md`, `./CLAUDE.local.md`. M4 consumes: run-the-first-experiment.md L21 and exercises/walk-and-send-off.md L40 name CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, memory, ADRs, authored skills; the consuming prompt walk-and-send-off-2 reads 'the ADRs in this repo, the skills at both `.claude/skills/` AND `~/.claude/skills/`' and its frontmatter `requires` names stride-adr and test-strategy-skill from the M3 prompts. Harm (silent missing artefact) absent: both ends resolve to a stable location. BACKWARD: every M4-consumed M3 item traces to an M3 row. Closest to violating: M4 body says 'any skills you've authored' (class, not path); the prompt carries the path. See suggestion on M3 L109 for the one promise with no consumer.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session boundaries and working directories are designed, not implicit.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Close: earn-the-trust.md L61-71 `## Clear the session` converge prompt then literal `/clear` (prompt ae101-m3-clear-session body `/clear`). Open: exercises/walk-and-send-off.md L5 `**Session** *(new, "Module 4 - Run the first experiment")*` and L11 'Start clean at your repo root', with the working-tree/branch check and rationale (closing `m4/<slug>` commit that M5 forks from). No directory change at this seam: M3 side-quest worktree is a sibling, M4 returns to the original repo root, so no 'same repo' ambiguity. Harm (student opens in the wrong folder, compounding branch confusion) absent. Closest to violating: 'your repo root' is not a literal path, but M3 Prework L10 fixed the repo as the one used since M1. Both directions walked.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cross-module artefact contracts — every produced file is a contract row in the maintainer block.
rules_evaluated.evidence: M3 maintainer block L182-188: three rows (ADR, test-strategy skill, CLAUDE.local.md) each with stable identifier, producing prompt/exercise, consuming module (M4 Phase 2 walk-and-fill named for all three). M4 maintainer block L158-164: three rows (m4/<task-slug> branch+SHA in task.md, observations/, transcript path) with producer and M5/M6 consumer. Harm (ambiguous identifier a judge cannot verify) absent. Closest to violating: ADR identifier is 'the repo's ADR convention; default docs/adr/NNNN-slug.md', a convention plus a default, which is unambiguous enough given the producing prompt discovers the convention. The M3 access map is scratch under $TMPDIR (map-the-access-surface.md L145), carries no repo path, and is exempt as a scrollback/scratch artefact.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cross-module structural-failure rescue — body-prose callouts at module open when the prior module's send-off can fail.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: M3 outputs come from in-room exercises, not an unwatched send-off; run-the-first-experiment.md `## Start here` L25-45 carries no rescue blockquote.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit-discipline — walk M(N-1) close + M(N) open before flagging M(N) architecture claims as spec drift.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: meta-rule for the auditor; three-surface walk performed for this pair in both directions and no spec-drift classification made.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Bring-or-scramble plain-stakes-line shape at module homework boundaries.
rules_evaluated.evidence: earn-the-trust.md L97 'Come to Module 4 without having picked the task and you'll be scrambling for one while the exercise is already running. Your call.' One sentence, student-as-subject, cost named against the exercise's clock not the room, choice preserved. None of the three failure modes: no M4 mechanics explained, no head-start prompt in the bring section, no unearned vocabulary. Harm (FOMO pressure, spoiled receiving beat) absent. Closest to violating: 'the exercise is already running' is the exercise clock form the rule endorses. M4's own L69 stakes line belongs to the M4->M5 pair, outside this set.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit-discipline — read every sibling exercise in a multi-exercise module before opining on one.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: read-only set check, proposes no change to a single exercise (the rule's own carve-out).
